summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for his fourth cycle of high-dose methotrexate reinduction therapy for recurrent central nervous system lymphoma. He reported continued improvement in his prior symptoms of headache and dizziness, with no new neurological deficits. The chemotherapy infusion was completed without acute complications. Methotrexate levels were monitored closely, with the 24-hour level at 2.3, requiring leucovorin rescue; levels declined appropriately to 0.08 by day four, allowing safe discontinuation of leucovorin. Mild transaminitis developed, consistent with prior cycles, and resolved during the admission. Constipation was managed with magnesium citrate and a new standing regimen of senna and docusate. GERD was managed with a temporary switch to ranitidine during treatment, with plans to resume omeprazole at discharge. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with oncology for scheduling of the next cycle.
problems: Other malignant lymphomas, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
